newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended strong, bouyed by hopes of an early interest rate cut after a worse-than-expected Q1 gross domestic product growth.
Gold shares ended flat, refusing to believe the platinum-inspired bullion price recovery was sustainable.

"The market firmed on expectations of a sooner rather than later cut in interest rates. The GDP figure shows that the economy is struggling a bit," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.
The Central Statistics Service said GDP fell a seasonally adjusted and annualised 0.8 percent in the first quarter of 1997 against a 3.3 percent rise in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast a first quarter rise of 2.5 percent.
Dealers said trade was volatile and thin but boosted by bookovers in Iscor and Barlows in the afternoon session. Iscor ended three cents up to 302 cents. Barlows rose 125 cents to 47.25 cents.
Some futures-related trade was also seen as players start preparing for the June futures close-out.
The market was seen sideways on Friday as players square positions ahead of the weekend.
The all-share index was gained 33.9 points to 7,074.7 points, the industrial index add 36.0 points to 8,317.9 points and the gold index rose 2.8 cents to 1,181.3 points.
Platinum shares continued to enjoy interest as the platinum price remains firm. Rusplats added 425 cents to 74.50 rand and Implats rose 200 cents to 46.50 rand.
Construction firm Group Five climbed 20 cents to 725 cents on Thursday after the company appointed a new chief executive officer.
Mast shares leap 14 cents to 110 cents after the company reported a 50 percent increase in interim profit compared to the 13 months ended August 31, 1996.
Near-dated share futures also bouyant on hopes of an early rate cut and a firm bond market. Gold contracts retreat to mark-to-market as market doubted the bullion price recovery.
The all-share contract was last at 6,440/45 from 6,365, the industrial contract was at 8,035/39 from 7,975 and the gold contract was at 829/35 from 828.
